summary: ARGUS-OS1 is an open-source centriole-age lineage tracking instrument led by Jaba Tqemaladze, MD, under the Georgia Longevity Alliance. The project combines a Rust-based agent core and an OpenFlexure-derived hardware platform to study OLD/NEW centriole inheritance in cellular aging. The document is primarily a project overview/landing page with no experimental results reported; data collection and preregistration are described as planned activities.

content_blocks.title: Project Overview — ARGUS-OS1
content_blocks.content: ARGUS-OS1 (open centriole-age lineage instrument) is a tool designed to track centriole age in cell lineages. Led by Jaba Tqemaladze, MD (Georgia Longevity Alliance). The project focuses on OLD/NEW centriole inheritance, a mechanism relevant to cellular aging and division orientation. No experimental results are reported in this document; the instrument and data pipeline are under development.

content_blocks.title: Software & Hardware Repositories
content_blocks.content: Two open-source repositories are listed: (1) Agent core written in Rust, licensed MIT, hosted at github.com/djabbat/argus-pre. (2) Hardware based on a fork of the OpenFlexure microscope project, licensed under CERN OHL-S. These indicate early-stage engineering development of the instrument platform, consistent with TRL 1–2.

content_blocks.title: Selected Publications — Scientific Basis
content_blocks.content:
Three publications are cited to establish the scientific foundation:
1. Tqemaladze 2023 (PubMed 36583780) — OLD/NEW centriole inheritance.
2. PubMed 38510429 — centriole biology and cellular aging.
3. PubMed 16336191 — division orientation in inheritance.
These publications provide the conceptual and prior-experimental basis for ARGUS-OS1 but are not results generated by the ARGUS-OS1 instrument itself.

content_blocks.title: Data & Reproducibility Plan (Planned)
content_blocks.content: The document outlines a planned open-science data pipeline: (1) Lineage dataset with full provenance to be deposited on Zenodo (DOI pending). (2) Preregistration on OSF (planned). (3) Protocols to be published on protocols.io. All items are explicitly marked as planned, indicating no data has been collected or published yet under this project.

content_blocks.title: IP & Licensing
content_blocks.content: Licensing structure: Code/models under Apache-2.0, hardware under CERN-OHL-S, data under CC-BY. IP is described as tokenized as a community-owned IPT (Intellectual Property Token) via VitaDAO/Molecule. No patents filed or granted are mentioned. This is a community/open-science IP model rather than a traditional patent-based approach.

content_blocks.title: Team & Affiliations
content_blocks.content: Lead researcher: Jaba Tqemaladze, MD. Affiliation: Georgia Longevity Alliance. ORCID: 0000-0001-8651-7243. Profiles on ResearchGate, X (djabbat1), and LinkedIn. Single named investigator; no additional team members, advisors, or institutional partners are listed.

key_findings: ARGUS-OS1 is an early-stage open-source instrument for centriole-age lineage tracking; no experimental results from the instrument are reported in this document.
Scientific basis rests on three prior publications (PubMed 36583780, 38510429, 16336191) covering OLD/NEW centriole inheritance and cellular aging — these predate the ARGUS-OS1 instrument.
Software (Rust, MIT-licensed) and hardware (OpenFlexure fork, CERN OHL-S) repositories exist, indicating active engineering development at TRL 1–2.
All data collection, Zenodo deposit, OSF preregistration, and protocols.io publication are explicitly described as planned — no data generated yet under this project.
IP is tokenized via VitaDAO/Molecule as a community-owned IPT; no traditional patents filed or granted.
Single-investigator project (Jaba Tqemaladze, MD, Georgia Longevity Alliance); no additional team, advisors, or institutional partners listed.
No funding amount, regulatory interactions, or clinical/preclinical studies are mentioned.
